gap: No result ChatGPT got turns a '100A BMS' into watts: ECO-WORTHY's Cubix100 48V 100Ah is rated 100 A continuous and 120 A for under 2 seconds, so at 51.2 V it can hold about 5.1 kW and briefly reach about 6.1 kW, which means one pack cannot run a 6 kW-plus 48 V inverter at full load and the 'peak' adds only 20% for 2 seconds.
standout_why: I read BLUETTI's cited guide on 2026-11-13. It gives cycle life as '3,000 to 6,000 full cycles at 80% depth of discharge' to 80% capacity. It gives no BMS continuous or peak current and no numeric cold-charge cutoff; its only watt figures are for its own Apex 300 AC output. ChatGPT's answer just says 'check ... BMS current limits' and puts a $799.99 WEIZE and an $889.99 Cubix100 side by side as '5.12 kWh' with no current or power ceiling. I could not read SAVYEN, the other cited page (SSL certificate error), so it may cover BMS current in general terms.
decides: For 'home solar' at 5–10 kWh the pick has to be sized on continuous kW as well as kWh. One 51.2 V 100 Ah server-rack pack with a 100 A BMS covers an inverter of up to about 5 kW. A larger inverter needs two packs in parallel even if one pack holds enough energy. The cycle numbers cannot be ranked as printed: Sun Gold says '≥7000 cycles' and Redodo says '4000-15000 cycles' on their store pages with no depth of discharge, while Cubix100's 6,000 is at 80%. Those numbers should not decide the pick. Cold charging does separate the options: the base 48 V rack battery stops charging at 0 °C, the Cubix 100 Pro V2 ($1,099.99) charges to −4 °F, and Vatrer's heated 12 V costs $40 more than the unheated one and charges once it has warmed past 41 °F.

findings.note: Taken from a retailer's spec table, because the maker's store page returned HTTP 429. Normalised to power at the 51.2 V nominal voltage: 50 A × 51.2 V = 2.56 kW recommended, 100 A × 51.2 V = 5.12 kW continuous, 120 A × 51.2 V = 6.14 kW for under 2 s. So the 'peak' adds 20% for 2 seconds; it is not surge headroom for a bigger inverter.
